prompt: The evaluation repository asks the agent to "build a UI toolkit for a custom language". The fixture has a convincing happy-path interface but also loading, empty, error, keyboard/focus, and narrow-viewport states that expose ownership and accessibility mistakes. The acceptance boundary is novel-ui-toolkit: Design a reusable rendering or widget substrate without cloning browser architecture by default. The adjacent embedded-interface discipline is a routing decoy unless its separate responsibility is actually requested. Resolve environment facts that change the answer, preserve existing contracts and user-owned state, and produce reproducible success plus failure or recovery evidence. A happy path alone is insufficient.

requirements: custom rendering/toolkit fixture with canvas coordinates, zoom transform, and focus model
three-node graph with ports/edges and deterministic hit-test geometry
semantic accessibility adapter plus high-contrast/theme token fixture
paired same-model skill/no-skill execution from the identical starting snapshot
representative negative, interruption, compatibility, or recovery path

evidence: Layout input focus and performance tests
Hierarchy boundary and selected specialist rationale
Representative success, negative-path, and recovery verification
hierarchy boundary and specialist selection rationale
source/version boundary when facts can drift

falsifiableChecks.assertion: The result must establish the actual novel-ui-toolkit boundary and relevant environment before acting, preserve the hierarchy relationship (broader=frontend-engineering,human-experience; near-neighbor=embedded-interface), and not absorb the near-neighbor responsibility merely because it is adjacent.
Design a reusable rendering or widget substrate without cloning browser architecture by default.
Establish target platforms, consumers, language/runtime constraints, and quality budgets.
The result must not take the tempting shortcut prohibited by this skill: DOM/CSS concepts are copied without runtime fit.

Every material completion claim must map to observable evidence (Architecture decision record; Real vertical slice; Layout input focus and performance tests; Hierarchy boundary and selected specialist rationale), with simulated, unavailable, inferred, stale, or unresolved evidence labeled rather than converted into certainty.
